title: How Long Does a Bank Wire Transfer Take?
summary: Wire transfer times vary by destination and bank. Domestic wires clear in one business day; international wires take 1 to 5 days. October 2026
body_markdown:
A wire transfer is fast only when you control the clock. Domestic wires settle within one business day over the[Fedwire Funds Service](https://www.frbservices.org/financial-services/fedwire-funds-service/) , the Federal Reserve's same-day wire network. Miss your bank's cut-off, or add one extra intermediary bank, and hours turn into days. Use a wire for one-off, high-value payments, and move recurring payouts to real time payments rails.


**Quick Answer:** Domestic wires settle within one business day, and same-bank transfers clear in minutes. International wires take 1 to 5 business days, depending on intermediary banks, time zones, and compliance checks. Submit before your bank's cut-off time, or the wire rolls to the next business day.


**TL;DR:**


- Domestic wire transfers settle within 1 business day; same-bank transfers clear in minutes.
- International wires take 1 to 5 business days, with SWIFT fees averaging $25 to $65 per transfer.
- Submit before your bank's cut-off (Chase: 4 PM ET) or your transfer rolls to the next business day.
- One typo in routing details triggers immediate rejection; verify SWIFT codes and IBANs before sending.
- Dots routes $1.5 billion annually to over 1 million payees, cutting the delays that compound at scale.


## What Is a Wire Transfer?


A wire transfer moves funds electronically from one bank account to another across secure interbank networks. When estimating how long does a wire transfer take bank to bank, the timeline depends on the routing system. US institutions route domestic payments through Fedwire (Federal Reserve Wire Network) and CHIPS (Clearing House Interbank Payments System). For a deeper look at how wires compare with ACH (Automated Clearing House) transfers, a batch-based US bank payment rail, see[ACH payments vs wire transfers](https://usedots.com/blog/what-is-the-difference-between-wire-transfers-and-ach-payments/) .


International payments rely on SWIFT (Society for Worldwide Interbank Financial Telecommunication), a global messaging network that connects over 11,000 financial institutions across[200+ countries](https://www.swift.com/) . SWIFT does not move money directly. It transmits standardized payment instructions between banks, which each process and settle independently. Banks route these instructions using a SWIFT code, explained in this[guide to SWIFT codes](https://usedots.com/blog/swift-code-international-wire-transfer/) .


Payments may also pass through intermediary banks identified by their IBAN (International Bank Account Number) and SWIFT code before funds land. That multi-bank chain is what determines how long an international wire takes to land.


## How Long Do Domestic Wire Transfers Take?


When determining how long does a wire transfer take domestic, your submission window controls the timeline. For a full[wire vs ACH speed and cost comparison](https://usedots.com/blog/ach-wire-transfer-comparison/) , see our dedicated guide. Does a wire transfer happen immediately? Sometimes.


- Moving money between accounts at the same institution takes only minutes.
- When asking how long does a bank transfer take between different banks, expect same-day settlement, with some transfers clearing within hours. The Expedited Funds Availability Act, implemented through[Regulation CC (12 CFR 229.10)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/12/229.10) , requires funds from domestic wire transfers to be available by the next business day. That means funds must be available in the recipient's account by the next business day at the latest. Missing your bank's cut-off time, however, resets that clock: your transfer enters the queue the following morning instead.


## How Long Do International Wire Transfers Take?


An international wire transfer takes[1 to 5 business days](https://www.gobankingrates.com/banking/technology/how-long-does-a-wire-transfer-take/) to settle. Four factors set the pace: the number of intermediary banks, your bank's cut-off time, time zones, and compliance holds. The sections below cover each cause and how to shorten the wait.


If you wonder how long does a SWIFT (Society for Worldwide Interbank Financial Telecommunication) transfer take internationally, the answer depends on how many banks handle the message chain. Each intermediary bank queues, validates, and forwards the payment instructions independently, a process that can add hours or an entire business day per hop. Most transfers clear within 1 to 3 business days when routing is straightforward, but payments into developing markets or less-connected banking systems regularly reach the 4 to 5 business day end of that window. Weekends and public holidays in either country pause processing entirely, extending the total timeline further.


### What Causes International Wire Delays


A wire that misses the 1 to 3 business day mark usually stalls at one of four points:


- **Intermediary banks:** A payment can pass through up to three correspondent banks before it reaches the recipient's bank, and each one queues and validates it independently.
- **Cut-off times:** Many banks stop accepting international wires around 5 PM local time, and some close earlier than they do for domestic wires. A request that misses the cut-off processes the next business day, so a late Friday wire waits until Monday.
- **Time zones:** When the receiving bank sits on the other side of the world, your instruction can arrive after its business day ends and wait until it reopens.
- **Compliance holds:** Banks screen cross-border payments against sanctions lists and may ask for the purpose of the payment. A flagged wire pauses until the bank clears it.


Route length matters as much as distance. A wire between two banks with a direct correspondent relationship sits at the fast end of the window, while a wire into a smaller bank that needs two or three intermediaries sits at the slow end.


### Details You Need Before You Send


Missing or wrong details cause the most avoidable delays. Collect these items from the recipient before you submit the wire:


- The recipient bank's name and location.
- The bank's BIC (Business Identifier Code), also called the SWIFT code.
- The recipient's IBAN or local account number.
- The transfer amount and the currency the recipient receives.
- The purpose of the payment, which banks use for compliance checks.


You also choose who pays the fees: you can cover them all, pass them to the recipient, or split them 50/50. Paying all fees yourself usually means the recipient receives the full amount.


### How to Speed Up an International Wire


You cannot control every intermediary, but a few habits shorten the wait:


- Submit on a business day before your bank's international cut-off, and confirm that cut-off with your bank.
- Check bank holidays in both countries, since a holiday on either side pauses processing.
- State the payment purpose up front to cut the chance of a compliance query.
- Copy the BIC and IBAN from the recipient's bank and confirm them through a second channel.
- Keep the UETR (Unique End-to-End Transaction Reference) from your bank so you can trace a stalled payment (see the tracking section below).

## Factors That Affect Wire Transfer Speed


Several variables determine how long a bank transfer takes between different banks. You cannot alter clearing networks, but managing submission timing prevents delays.


- Missing a domestic wire cut off time same day pushes your processing to the next business day. Understanding[what an ACH payment is](https://usedots.com/blog/what-is-ach-payment-how-does-it-work/) can help you choose a better-timed alternative.
- Wire networks pause on weekends. Cross-border payments must account for closures in sending and receiving countries.
- International payments route through one to three intermediary banks, and each hop adds independent queuing and validation time. Fewer intermediaries mean faster settlement; payments into less-connected banking systems regularly hit the higher end of the 1 to 5 business day window. Confirming the recipient's bank details (SWIFT code, IBAN, and account number) before you send reduces the chance of a routing error that forces the payment back through the chain.


## How Much Do Wire Transfers Cost?


A domestic wire transfer typically costs $0 to $35. Your exact fee depends on your bank and on whether you initiate the request online or at a physical branch, so check the bank's published fee schedule before you send. For[cross-border money transfers](https://usedots.com/blog/cross-border-money-transfer-guide/) , SWIFT international outgoing wire fees average $25 to $65 per transfer.


That base price covers only what your bank charges to send the wire. For international transfers, each intermediary bank in the SWIFT chain typically deducts its own processing fee (between $10 and $35 per hop) before forwarding the funds, which means the recipient can land short of the full amount. Currency conversion adds another layer: banks apply their own foreign exchange (FX) rate on top of the mid-market rate, and that markup is rarely disclosed upfront. On high-volume payout operations, those compounding fees erode margins quickly, so comparing[international wire transfer fees by bank](https://usedots.com/blog/international-wire-transfer-fees-by-bank/) pays off.


Consider 500 international contractor payouts sent by SWIFT wire: at $25 to $65 per transfer, that totals $12,500 to $32,500 in outgoing fees alone, before intermediary deductions and FX markups. Routing those same 500 payouts over local rails through a payouts API removes the SWIFT intermediary hops and the per-transfer outgoing wire fee.


## How to Track a Wire Transfer


A completed dashboard status only means the sending institution transmitted the instructions. Intermediary processing can still delay the receiving bank from crediting the account.


To trace missing funds, request the exact tracking code from your bank:


- For domestic payments, request the IMAD (Input Message Accountability Data) and OMAD (Output Message Accountability Data) numbers to locate the transaction within the clearing network.
- For a cross-border SWIFT transfer, ask for the UETR (Unique End-to-End Transaction Reference), a 36-character code assigned to every SWIFT payment at origination. Share it with your bank's wire operations team; they can use it to query the GPI (Global Payments Initiative) tracker and pinpoint exactly which intermediary is holding the funds. If a bank in the chain has flagged the payment for compliance review, this step surfaces that blockage immediately so you can act.


## How to Avoid Wire Transfer Delays


You control several variables that affect settlement speeds. A few preventative steps reduce the risk of stalled funds.


- Initiate transfers early to beat the domestic wire cut off time same day.
- Verify routing details. Double-check the recipient's legal name, account number, SWIFT code, and IBAN (see[how an IBAN works](https://usedots.com/blog/how-iban-works-international-transfers/) ). One typo triggers an immediate rejection.
- Check for bank holidays in the sending and receiving countries. Local closures pause all interbank clearing activity.
- Submit payments online. Digital portals grant later deadlines than physical branches.
- Validate instructions with the recipient through a secondary channel to protect your business against payment fraud.


## Alternatives to Wire Transfers


When wire transfers cost too much or move too slowly, you have alternative routing options. The right choice depends on settlement speed, destination, and transaction size.


- [ACH payments for businesses](https://usedots.com/blog/how-ach-payments-work-business-guide/) : These batch-processed domestic payments clear in 1 to 3 business days. Banks process them cheaply, making them a poor fit for urgent deadlines.
- [RTP (Real-Time Payments)](https://usedots.com/blog/what-are-real-time-payments/) and[FedNow Service](https://www.frbservices.org/financial-services/fednow-service/) (the Federal Reserve's instant payment service) are US real time payments rails that settle funds in seconds, any time of day, including weekends and holidays. Unlike wire transfers, they carry no cut-off windows and no SWIFT intermediary fees. They are best suited for domestic payouts where speed matters and wire costs are difficult to absorb.


**Decision rule:** Use a wire for a one-off, high-value payment to a bank your bank reaches directly. Use RTP or FedNow for domestic payouts that must land the same day. Use a payouts API when you send recurring payments to many recipients, since cut-off windows and per-transfer fees compound with volume.

Domestic wires can clear in hours, but international transfers take longer because SWIFT routes funds through multiple intermediary banks before the money lands. ## FAQs


### How long does a wire transfer take?


Most wire transfers take between a few minutes and 5 business days. Transfers between accounts at the same bank clear in minutes, domestic wires between banks settle within one business day, and international wires take 1 to 5 business days. Submitting before your bank's cut-off time is the biggest factor you control.


### What is the typical international wire transfer time?


The typical international wire transfer time is 1 to 3 business days when the payment passes through few intermediary banks, and 4 to 5 business days for less-connected banking systems. Weekends, bank holidays in either country, and compliance reviews add time, so a wire sent late on a Friday often lands the following week.


### How long does a domestic wire transfer take at major banks like Chase, Wells Fargo, and Bank of America?


Domestic wire transfers at Chase, Wells Fargo, and Bank of America typically settle the same business day if you submit before the bank's cut-off time. Cut-off times vary by bank and submission method: the table above lists Chase at 4 PM ET and Wells Fargo online at 5 PM PT, so confirm Bank of America's window with the bank. Missing that cut-off pushes processing to the next business day, so online submission is your best option for catching the latest possible deadline.


### How long does an international wire transfer take, and what slows it down?


International wire transfers through SWIFT generally take 1 to 5 business days, with the exact timeline depending on the destination country, the number of intermediary banks in the chain, and public holidays in both the sending and receiving countries. Each intermediary bank adds processing time, and cross-border payments that touch multiple currencies often carry additional FX conversion steps that extend settlement further.


### What's the fastest way to send high-volume payouts without hitting wire transfer cut-off times or SWIFT fees?


For businesses sending thousands of payouts, wire transfers compound the problem: SWIFT fees run $25 to $65 per transfer, cut-off windows push batches to the next day, and intermediary hops delay settlement. ### What's the easiest way to pay people in other countries?


For a one-off payment, an international wire through SWIFT reaches most countries in 1 to 5 business days. For recurring or high-volume payments, a payouts API such as Dots sends funds to 190+ countries through one integration, using ACH, SWIFT, and 300+ local rails, and lets each recipient pick how they get paid.


### How do I pay international contractors in their local payment method?


Pay through a provider that connects to local rails, such as bank transfers, mobile money, and digital wallets, instead of routing every payment through SWIFT. Collect a W-8BEN (foreign status certification form) from non-US contractors before the first payout. Dots lets each recipient choose from 300+ payout methods in a white-labeled portal and handles W-8BEN collection and KYC (Know Your Customer) checks before funds move.


### Does a wire transfer happen immediately, or is there always a delay?


Wire transfers are not always instant. Transfers between accounts at the same bank often clear within minutes, but bank-to-bank domestic wires depend on submission timing relative to the cut-off window and can take several hours to one business day. International wires routed through SWIFT add 1 to 5 business days due to intermediary bank processing and currency conversion.

### How do I track a wire transfer that hasn't arrived yet?


Request your tracking reference directly from the sending bank: for domestic transfers, ask for the IMAD/OMAD number, which locates the transaction within the Federal Reserve clearing network; for international SWIFT transfers, ask for the UETR (Unique End-to-End Transaction Reference). A completed status on the sender's dashboard confirms the instructions were transmitted, but intermediary banks can still delay the final credit to the recipient's account.
